TABRISI, d. 548 (author): All beautiful praise belongs to God, who deserves worship as the source of original blessings and the creator, nurturer, and reformer of creation; the verse teaches gratitude and praise. TABRISI, d. 548 (author): Al-ʿālamīn has no singular of the same form and may derive from the mark by which creation points to its Maker, or from knowledge as what is known. RAZI, d. 606 (author): “Lord” is in a genitive construction with “the worlds” as its genitive complement; understanding this relation requires knowing both terms. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 (author): The phrase al-ḥamdu lillāh raises questions about God’s existence and right to praise; Rabb al-ʿālamīn answers the first, while al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, and Mālik yawm al-dīn answer the second.
